newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher in active trading on Tuesday following the Bank of Israel's decision to reduce its key interest rate, traders said.
On Monday, after the close of trading, the central bank said it was lowering its key lending rate for February by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 14.2 percent.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 102.07
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct to 101.30.
Volume was moderate at 133 million shekels with turnover in the Makam rising to 60 million shekels.

"The rate cut was within expectations but it is clear that in the long run the Bank of Israel will have to continue to reduce interest rates," said Yigal Mizrahi, chief analyst at Nesuah Trading and Investments.
"Desite that, the bond market reacted favourably to the reduction and long-CPI-linked bonds, Makams and unlinked bonds rose," Mizrahi said.

"Inflation-linked bonds continued to rise. Investors believe that in the long run, interest rates will continue to fall and inflation will decline as well," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
"Unlinked bonds and Makams reacted very nicely to the rate cut. Activity in the Makam rose sharply despite the fact that yields (on the one year Makam) fell to 13.8 percent," Mizrahi said.
Dollar-linked bonds rose sharply as the shekel fell to a new all-time low against the dollar following the rise of the U.S. currency on overseas markets.
In the local foreign currency market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at an all-time high of 3.3190 shekels against 3.3060 shekels on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
